instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Hidden Power
cards.instruction: Act publicly modest while making choices as though you control the outcome.

cards.title: Supportive Rage
cards.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only fetching the cloths. You've got paint on my sofa, but stay there; I'll choose a clean bit and we'll get it off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the carpet too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep blotting. You're doing well. That carpet was my birthday present; I'll deal with the sofa before I look at it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This cloth's spreading the paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. Take my clean shirt for the carpet; I'll find something else for the sofa. My bloody birthday carpet. Keep going, you're not doing this alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only doing the driving today. Choose the birthday lunch you really want; I've cleared the afternoon for it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The seaside place. We'd lose your deposit here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forty pounds wasted. Fine, I'll cancel here and we'll leave at ten. You deserve a whole day by the sea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it. They need another forty now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eighty pounds before a bloody sandwich. Give me the number; I'll pay and get us a window table. You're having the sea view, not the kitchen door.

cards.title: Terms and Conditions
cards.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I only keep the shed tidy. I'll get you the ladder for two lifts to the station.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need it for five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One lift, then. I'll leave it by your gate once you've told your wife my roses are improving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just pay you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five pounds. Three if you say we're still friends when you hand it over. I'll bring the ladder round as soon as we've settled that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only keeping the family diary. I'll accept your apology for missing my birthday if I choose when you visit at Christmas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum already expects me on Christmas Day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put you here for Boxing Day, then. In return, I'll tell her I'm no longer hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather you actually stopped being hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay through New Year and I'll mean it. I'll leave your room made up until then, and take the birthday out of my calls to Mum.

cards.title: Yes, but My Way
cards.instruction: Agree with others, then reinterpret the agreement entirely in your favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only a spare pair of hands. Yes, I'll help with the sofa; I'll take the cushions while you lift the rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're sewn on. We have to lift together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. I'll say three, and you lift on three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need another person underneath it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll book someone on your phone and choose a time we're both here. Then I can give you both the same countdown.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's only a little dog-sitting. Yes, bring him over after his walk; I'll decide where his bed goes while your kitchen's being repaired.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He needs to stay overnight too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. I'll put you in the guest room beside him, so you can give him breakfast while I sleep.

beats.text: I can stay, but his six o'clock walk is your job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll organise it: lead by the door, your alarm at five thirty. I'll put your shoes out too, so you won't have to plan a thing.

cards.title: The Pattern
cards.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only filling the biscuit tin. Two have gone already; I'll hand the rest out myself. This looks organised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ate them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A confession that quick suggests training. I'll keep the tin on my desk while we establish who's involved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they're recruiting through hunger. I'll choose everyone's lunch today; whoever objects to being fed goes on our list of organisers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only passing the meeting details on, but nobody received my email. I'll put everything on hold; communication here has broken down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in your drafts. You forgot to send it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And nobody noticed. I'll introduce a second check before any office message goes out; the whole system can't depend on my memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send it. Go and have your lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're covering communications in my absence. I'll name a deputy for you before I go; we need a succession plan, not just a sandwich break.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only passing the tools. Could you hold this shelf bracket against the holes while I choose the right screw?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Briefly. I'm dressed for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This top one will hold it. Could you turn it once? I'll keep the rest ready, then you can let go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's holding. The other screws are already lined up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just tighten those, then? I'll put the shelf beside you; slide it on to check it fits, and I'll fetch your coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only holding the wedding ribbon. Could you pinch these bouquet stems together while I choose where the bow goes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got them. They need wire underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, we'll put it under your fingers. Could you just twist this piece round? I'll keep the ribbon out of your way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. The sharp end will snag the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tuck that in and wind the ribbon over it? A little bow on this side would hide the join. I'll hold the scissors while you finish it.
